subject: Post-call: MonetaPay unit-cost framing & pilot gating questions
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Ivanov <sasha@monetapay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Mar 2028 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: MonetaPay unit-cost framing & pilot gating questions

Hi Sasha — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we have alignment before I put together an SOW.

TL;DR
- Primary pain: inference costs spike unpredictably on peak flows (chat + structured extraction); current infra is absorbing cost but the product margin is at risk.
- Goal: prove a 2-week pilot that shows a repeatable path to unit economics that meet MonetaPay’s target and preserves ~100ms median latency for primary chat flows.
- Requested from you: confirmation on pilot budget ceiling and any procurement constraints (timelines, required paperwork).

Key notes from call
- Workload: conversational chat + small NER/label extraction. Expected pilot traffic ~60–120k calls/day (burst to 250k) with average prompt+completion tokens of ~220 tokens.
- SLA/latency: product team needs ~100–200ms p50 for chat. They are flexible on p95 if cost savings materialize.
- Budget guardrail: you mentioned an initial pilot budget that needs to sit below a monthly run-rate threshold — can you confirm a hard ceiling for the POC? We framed a baseline target of ~$25k-$40k/month equivalent for the production footprint; pilot should demonstrate a credible path under that.

Redwood recommendations we discussed (for the POC)
1) Model variant + quantization: start with a 4-bit quantized generalist model for completions to cut unit cost ~25–35% versus FP16 while keeping latency acceptable.
2) Batching & continuous KV caching: expected 3–6x effective token cost reduction on your workload shape; we’ll simulate with your prompt mix.
3) Prefix/prompt caching for common templates: should reduce repeated prompt tokens by up to 40% for the top 20% of requests.
4) Routing fallback: run a canary serving on a lower-cost variant for non-critical flows (e.g., NER) to protect latency-sensitive chat.

Attachments I’ll include in the SOW: redwood-pilot-sow.pdf (draft SOW), estimated-econ.xlsx (baseline token-econ scenarios). I also attached a short simulation plan in batching-simulations.csv for your ops team to review.

Action items (next steps)
- Sasha / Priya: confirm pilot budget ceiling and procurement timeline for a 2-week POC (reply here).
- MonetaPay: send sample prompt distribution (anonymized) for more accurate batching sims — if possible by EOD Friday.
- Redwood (Marissa/Aditya): draft SOW and cost scenarios; Marissa will lead pricing.

If we get budget and sample prompts this week I can have a draft SOW and a preliminary econ model back to you by Monday.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0118

- estimated-econ.xlsx (baseline scenarios)

Date: Thu, 2 Mar 2028 09:34:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: MonetaPay unit-cost framing & pilot gating questions

Thanks Rachel — helpful summary. Confirming a few things from our side.

- Budget ceiling for pilot: our procurement lead gave an internal cap of $30k for the 2-week POC (that includes any service fees). We need to see credible modeling that shows expected monthly run-rate at production scale (100k DAU) can be pushed under ~$35k/month (target).
- Token visibility: we can provide an anonymized prompt sample set (~5k calls) by Friday. Security: SOC2 + encryption-at-rest are must-haves before production; for the POC we can run under NDA if SOC2 evidence is delayed.
- Latency tolerance: product team reiterated p50 ~120ms target for chat; p95 can be up to 1s for now.

A few asks: can you produce one realistic example (1 page) that shows the delta between no-batching baseline and an expected 4x batching outcome for our prompt shapes? Also include an example of how prefix caching would change token counts for the top 10 templates.

We can target a pilot kickoff the week of Mar 13 if procurement moves quickly — procurement will need a 5–7 business day review on an SOW / PO.

Date: Fri, 3 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: MonetaPay unit-cost framing & pilot gating questions

Thanks Sasha — good constraints, and helpful on timeline. Quick follow-up with concrete framing so procurement has something to review.

Pilot hypothesis (what we’ll prove in 2 weeks)- With batching (4x median effective batch size) + prefix caching for repeated templates + 4-bit quantization we can reduce your token spend by ~55–65% versus the current unbatched FP16 baseline on the sample mix you described. That puts modeled run-rate for a 100k DAU production footprint below your $35k/month target in our scenarios (see attached estimated-econ.xlsx for detailed scenarios).

Concrete levers we’ll operate in the POC
- Batching: client-aware continuous batching (we expect 3–6x depending on seq distribution). For your prompt mix we simulated a median effective batch of 4.
- Prefix caching: identify top 10 templates >40% repeat factor; cache prefix tokens and rewrite requests to minimize repeated prompt tokens.
- Model quant: 4-bit Q4 into our optimized runtime; expected 30% less token cost and ~10–20ms p50 increase (within your tolerance).

Example deliverables for procurement review (we will include these in SOW)
1) One-page econ snapshot: baseline vs batching vs batching+cache+quant (attachment: estimated-econ.xlsx, tab "OnePage").
2) Simulation outputs from your sample prompts (attachment: batching-simulations.csv).
3) Pilot runbook: configuration, observability checkpoints, rollback triggers (attachment: redwood-pilot-sow.pdf).

Proposed schedule
- Fri Mar 3: MonetaPay sends anonymized prompt sample (5k).
- Mon Mar 6: Redwood returns preliminary batching sims + 1-page econ snapshot.
- Tue Mar 7: 30-min sync to review scenarios (we propose 10am PT).
- Week of Mar 13: Pilot kickoff (contingent on PO/SOW approval).

Open asks for your procurement team
- Confirm the $30k cap for the 2-week POC (we will price the SOW to fit that cap).
- Confirm whether MonetaPay needs a PO (preferred) or if a signed SOW is sufficient to start.
- Timeline for SOC2 evidence review; if we can provide limited access under NDA that would accelerate start.

Action owners
- Rachel: deliver sims + one-page econ (by Mon 3/6).
- Marissa: finalize pricing bands and POC invoice schedule.
- Aditya: validate runtime config and expected latency uplift on quant runs.

If that looks good I’ll produce a short SOW and SOW + pricing addendum for procurement to review.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Hi all — procurement here. Quick notes so we can move this forward: 

1) Confirmed: we can allocate up to $30k for a 2-week POC provided the SOW clearly caps spend and lists acceptance criteria (economics threshold + no-regression on p50 latency).
2) Docs: we require SOC2 evidence before production but can accept NDA + limited access for a POC. Please attach SOC2 snapshot or a SOC2 letter to the SOW where possible.
3) PO vs SOW: Procurement prefers a PO for any paid POC. If Redwood needs a signed SOW first, procurement can issue a PO conditioned on the signed SOW within 5 business days.
4) Redlines: we will circulate a single-page procurement checklist (procurement@monetapay.com) — please expect it by EOD Mon.

Next steps
- Rachel / Marissa: please send a 1-page econ snapshot and the SOW draft (redwood-pilot-sow.pdf) so we can start legal review.
- Procurement will review and return checklist + redlines by Mon EOD.

Thanks —
Priya Menon
